title: Lesson 30 - Files, Knowledge, and Custom Metadata/Settings Security
description: Given a scenario, determine the appropriate access control to grant access to files, Knowledge articles, and custom metadata/settings (data outside standard/custom objects).

questions.question: A user can open an Account record but cannot see a file attached to it. What is the most likely reason?
options: File access is governed separately from record access - the file isn't shared with that user
The Account is a master record
questions.explanation: File sharing is independent of record sharing; a file attached to a record is only visible to users the file is shared with (via sharing settings, libraries, or record sharing when configured). Record access alone does not grant file access.

questions.question: Which mechanism controls which Knowledge articles a user can view?
options: Article visibility (internal/customer) plus data category security plus the View Articles permission
questions.explanation: Knowledge article visibility combines the user's Knowledge permission with internal/customer visibility and data categories. It is not record-owner or OWD driven.

questions.question: Which statement about custom metadata types is TRUE?
options: They are governed by record sharing rules
They are typically configuration visible to users granted the relevant object permission, protected by the Protected flag in managed packages, and do not follow OWD/sharing
They are always public to all users
questions.explanation: Custom metadata is configuration metadata, not record data; its access is via object permissions and the Protected flag, not the OWD/sharing model.
